causality: bar-t features activate for the t+1 return; settled funding is event-time information and activates no earlier than the next hour; no returns bridge source gaps

families.hypothesis: Extreme settled funding predicts a crowded-position reversal.
families.economic_story: Funding transfers balance crowded perpetual demand; extremes can identify vulnerable positioning, not a free carry claim.
families.falsifier: Nonpositive at 10bps, fewer than two positive thirds, fewer than two assets, or extra-bar delay is as good or better.

families.hypothesis: Fixed 168h momentum persists more when funding is not extreme.
families.economic_story: Trend with modest leverage demand may be less crowded than trend accompanied by funding extremes.
families.falsifier: The conditioned rule does not clear base costs/cross-asset tests or the condition adds no useful robustness.

families.hypothesis: Extreme premium-index levels predict subsequent perpetual mean reversion.
families.economic_story: Premium is a direct measure of perp-index dislocation and an input to anchoring pressure.
families.falsifier: No lagged net relation after cost, or only contemporaneous premium convergence.

families.hypothesis: Taker-buy quote-volume imbalance forecasts continuation or reversal at the next bar.
families.economic_story: Aggressive flow can reflect information or temporary pressure; both signs are predeclared.
families.falsifier: The next-bar effect vanishes after costs, cross-asset checks, or an extra-bar delay.

classification: INTERESTING requires positive 10bps net, at least two positive thirds, support on at least two assets, and real alignment beating the extra-bar-delay diagnostic. It remains exploratory; no formal inference is attempted.
